Learn how to customize the theme of the Vonage Video Android App.

Welcome! In this tutorial you will customize the theme of the **Vonage Video Android App** (`vonage-video-android-app`), a Kotlin application built with Gradle. Building and running it natively requires **Android Studio Ladybug (2024.2.1)+**, **JDK 17+**, and an emulator or physical device — none of which this Codespace has. So instead of editing and building here, you will clone the repo to your own machine and do all of that work there.

This Codespace's only job is to run the shared Node.js backend server that the Android app talks to, and to expose its port so your locally-running app can reach it.

## In this tutorial you will

- Start the shared backend server in this Codespace and make its port public
- Clone `vonage-video-android-app` to your own machine and run it in Android Studio against that backend
- Explore how color, border radius, and typography tokens are structured in `config/theme.json`
- Edit theme tokens and regenerate the corresponding Compose theme resources
- Rebuild the app and confirm your changes in the Android emulator

{% aside type="caution" %}
This Codespace cannot run Android Studio or an emulator. You cannot build, run, or preview the Android app here — everything you do in this Codespace is limited to running the backend server. Building and verifying the app happens in Android Studio on your own machine.
{% /aside %}

{% aside %}
Looking to enable or disable app features instead? See the companion **Vonage Video Android App Feature Config** tutorial.
{% /aside %}

Let's start by setting up the backend server and getting the app running locally.

The Android app doesn't have a backend of its own — it talks to the same Node.js server the Vonage Video React App uses, running on port **3345**. In this step you will start that backend here in the Codespace, expose its port publicly, then clone the Android app to your own machine and run it in Android Studio against that public URL.

## Configure Backend Credentials

Open a terminal inside the Codespace by clicking the **hamburger menu (☰)** in the top-left corner, then selecting **Terminal → New Terminal**. The cloned repo lives under `project/`, so run all commands below from there:

```sh
cd project
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
code backend/.env
```

Replace the placeholder values in `backend/.env`:

```sh
# backend/.env
VONAGE_APP_ID=your-vonage-application-id
VONAGE_PRIVATE_KEY='-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
...
-----END PRIVATE KEY-----
'
```

| Variable             | Where to find it                                                                                            |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

The Android app's visual theme lives in a single JSON file in your local clone: **`config/theme.json`**. This is the file you'll edit to customize colors, corner rounding, and typography without touching any Kotlin or Compose source code.

## Where It Lives

{% filetree %}

- config/
  - app-config.json
  - theme.json   ← Theme tokens live here
- app/
- vonage-video-ui-compose/
- ...

{% /filetree %}

## How It's Structured

`theme.json` nests every token under `themes.vonage`, split into three groups: `colors`, `borderRadius`, and `typography`:

```json
{
  "themes": {
    "vonage": {
      "colors": {
        "light": { "primary": "#9941FF", "background": "#F5F0FD", "...": "..." },
        "dark":  { "primary": "#B377FF", "background": "#1C1C1E", "...": "..." }
      },
      "borderRadius": {
        "none": 0, "extra-small": 2, "small": 4, "medium": 8, "large": 12, "extra-large": 24
      },
      "typography": {
        "font-family": "Inter",
        "desktop": { "headline": { "font-size": "66px", "line-height": "88px", "font-weight": 500 }, "...": "..." },
        "mobile":  { "headline": { "font-size": "32px", "line-height": "40px", "font-weight": 500 }, "...": "..." }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`colors.light` / `colors.dark`** — Separate color palettes for each mode. Both modes use the same set of semantic token keys, including `on-*` pairs (e.g. `on-primary`) for text/icon color placed on top of that token.
- **`borderRadius`** — Six named tokens controlling the corner rounding of buttons, cards, and dialogs.
- **`typography`** — `desktop` and `mobile` type scales. Both scales use the same named tokens, just with different point sizes.

## Color Token Reference

Here's the subset of color tokens you'll work with most often:

| Token | Light default | Dark default | Role |
|-------|--------------|--------------|------|
| `primary` | `#9941FF` | `#B377FF` | Main brand accent |
| `on-primary` | `#FFFFFF` | `#000000` | Text/icons drawn on top of `primary` |
| `secondary` | `#000000` | `#FFFFFF` | Secondary accent |
| `background` | `#F5F0FD` | `#1C1C1E` | Page background |
| `surface` | `#FFFFFF` | `#2C2C2E` | Cards and panels |
| `text-primary` | `#9941FF` | `#B377FF` | Primary text |
| `error` | `#E61D1D` | `#FF6B6B` | Errors and destructive actions |
| `warning` | `#BE5702` | `#FF9F4A` | Warnings |
| `success` | `#1C8731` | `#4CD964` | Confirmations |
| `border` | `#E6E6E6` | `#3A3A3C` | Dividers and borders |
| `disabled` | `#E6E6E6` | `#3A3A3C` | Disabled control backgrounds |
